Every statement is an IMPORTED_PREPRINT claim (unrefereed, AI-generated, no Lean). (1) Goldfeld2, preprints/Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026/build/sections/00-introduction.tex:35-46, \begin{theorem}[Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture]\label{thm:main-density}: 'For every elliptic curve $E/\Q$ and each $j\in\{0,1\}$, \lim_{X\to\infty} \#\{d\in\mathcal D(X):a(E^{(d)})=j\}/\#\mathcal D(X) = 1/2. Consequently the twists of analytic rank at least two have density zero. For a density-one set of signed squarefree parameters $d$, the analytic and Mordell--Weil ranks of $E^{(d)}$ agree and its whole Tate--Shafarevich group is finite.' Here (lines 26-30) '$\mathcal D(X)=\{d\in\Z:0<|d|\le X,\ d\text{ squarefree}\}$', $a(E)=\ord_{s=1}L(E,s)$, $c_2(E)=\corank_{\Ztwo}\Sel_{2^\infty}(E/\Q)$ (lines 3-7). Hypotheses: none beyond E/Q elliptic. Its only pointwise ingredient is Thm 1.1 (lines 15-20) \label{thm:main-converse}: 'For every elliptic curve $E/\Q$ with $c_2(E)\in\{0,1\}$, $a(E)=r(E)=c_2(E)$, $\Sha(E/\Q)$ is finite.' and 01-preliminaries.tex:12-25 \label{pr:ranks}: '$c_2(A)=r(A)+\corank_{\Ztwo}\Sha(A/\Q)[2^\infty]$. If $a(A)\le1$, then $r(A)=a(A)$, the whole group $\Sha(A/\Q)$ is finite, and $c_2(A)=a(A)$.' Parity: 01-preliminaries.tex:40-52 \label{pr:invariance}: '$(-1)^{c_2(A)}=\varepsilon(A)$ ... $\corank_{\Ztwo}\Sel_{2^\infty}(A/K)=c_2(A)+c_2(A^{(k)})$.' Disclaimer 00-introduction.tex:90-91: 'The rank and finiteness assertions are distinct from the Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer leading-coefficient formula.' (2) MeanRank, preprints/The-mean-analytic-rank-of-quadratic-twists-of-elliptic-curves-October-6-2026/build/sections/introduction.tex:50-58, \begin{theorem}\label{thm:tail}: 'For every elliptic curve $E/\Q$, there are constants $C_E>0$ and an integer $R_E\ge1$ such that, for every integer $R\ge R_E$, \limsup_{Y\to\infty}\frac1Y \sum_{d\in\mathcal D(Y),\ a(E^{(d)})>R} a(E^{(d)}) \le C_E/R.' Also introduction.tex:22-28 \label{thm:mean}: mean analytic rank $=1/2$. Supporting: tail.tex:16-27 \label{tail:count}: 'There are $k_0$, $X_0$, and $C$, depending on $E$, such that for every $F\in\mathcal F$, every dyadic $X\ge X_0$, and every integer $k_0+1\le k\le(\log X)^{3/5}$, one has $\#\{d\in\mathcal A(X):a(F^{(d)})>k\}\le CXk^{-2}$.' tail.tex:115-120 \label{tail:jensen}: 'Uniformly for $F\in\mathcal F$ and $d\in\mathcal A(X)$, $a(F^{(d)})\ll_E\log(3X)$.' weights.tex:50-83 \label{weights:vanishing} (Completed derivative identity): with $g_d(z)=L_{F^{(d)}}(1/2+z)(C_F|d|)^z\Gamma(1+z)$, $\epsilon_d=\operatorname{sign}(F^{(d)})$: '$g_d$ is entire, $g_d(-z)=\epsilon_d g_d(z)$, and $\mathcal S_d := \sum_{n\ge1}\lambda(n)\chi_d(n)n^{-1/2}W_{k,x}(\ell^{-1}\log n) = \frac{k!}{\ell^k}\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{(2)}g_d(z)\,dz/z^{k+1}$. More precisely, $(1+\epsilon_d(-1)^k)\mathcal S_d=\ell^{-k}g_d^{(k)}(0)$. Consequently, if $a(F^{(d)})>k$ and $\epsilon_d=(-1)^k$, then [the weighted sum] $=0$.' The threshold is forced by model.tex:265 'after requiring $\sqrt{k_0}\ge256$' (so $k_0\ge 65536$, hence $R_E\ge k_0+1$ by tail.tex:171), model.tex:215 '$k_0\ge(8C_{\rm len}/\eta)^4$', weights.tex:188 '$k_0\ge r+2$'. hypotheses_check: K-RANK2 applied. For E (seed): rank E(Q)=2 (basis P1=(4547,327384), P2=(5184,281520), saturated), so by the Kummer sequence $s_p(E)=\corank\Sel_{p^\infty}(E/\Q)\ge2$ at EVERY prime p, in particular $c_2(E)\ge2$. Hence Goldfeld2 Thm 1.1 (needs $c_2\in\{0,1\}$), Pointwise2 Thm 1.1 (needs $E(\Q)[2]\ne0$ -- which holds, $T=(0,0)$ -- AND $s_2\in\{0,1\}$ -- which fails), SelmerConverse Thm 1.1 (needs $s_p\in\{0,1\}$), TwoPrimary Thm 1.1 and ExactBSD Thm 1.1 (need $s_q\in\{0,1\}$ for some q) all FAIL at every prime for E: p=2 ($s_2\ge2$; note $\Sha[2^\infty]=0$ so $s_2=2$ exactly), p=3 ($s_3=2$ exactly since $\Sha[3^\infty]\cong(\Z/3)^2$ is finite), p=2243, 4547, 5843 ($s_p\ge2$; equality unknown pending FIN at those p), good ordinary and good supersingular p ($s_p\ge2$; $=2$ for good $5\le p\le47$ by the lab's settled $\Sha[p^\infty]=0$ there, unknown beyond). No reduction-type, CM, torsion, isogeny or $\bar\rho$ hypothesis appears in any of these theorems, so the recorded $\bar\rho_p(G_\Q)\supseteq SL_2(\F_p)$ at p in {2243,5843} and its absence elsewhere are irrelevant. Goldfeld2 Thm 1.2 and MeanRank Thm 1.1/1.2 have NO pointwise hypothesis: they hold for every E/Q, so the seed E satisfies them trivially -- but their conclusions concern the family $\{E^{(d)}\}$ counted by |d| <= X and say nothing about the single member d=1 except that it belongs to the density-zero set of twists with $a\ge2$ (which the lab already knows: $a(E)\ge2$ is PROVED via Kolyvagin/Kato + sign +1). Parity statements (Goldfeld2 \label{pr:invariance}: $(-1)^{c_2}=\varepsilon$) are consistent with the seed ($c_2(E)=2$ even, $w(E)=+1$) and add nothing; they are published (Dokchitser--Dokchitser 2010 / Monsky at 2). For E^{-7}: $s_p(E^{-7})=0$ for all p (rank 0 and Sha finite by Gross--Zagier--Kolyvagin from $L(E^{-7},1)\ne0$, PROVED_COMPUTER_ASSISTED interval [9.054319, 9.054421]), so the corank-<=1 theorems' hypotheses HOLD for E^{-7} at every p including the additive primes 2, 4547, 7 (conductor 49N) -- but their rank/finiteness conclusions are already known for E^{-7} by GZK and the leading-term assertions belong to the separate candidate twist-E-7 (scan/assess/twist-E-7.json), not to this item. MeanRank Lemma weights:vanishing (the Mellin identity) is an identity valid for any d with the paper's normalization; at d=1, k=2, $\epsilon=+1$ it reads $2\mathcal S_1=\ell^{-2}g_1''(0)$ with $g_1(z)=L(E,1/2+z)\cdot N^{z}\Gamma(1+z)$ in the center-1/2 normalization, i.e. the standard smoothed series for $\Lambda''(E,1)$ -- the lab already uses this numerically; it is a textbook consequence of the functional equation (BCDT modularity), not a new input.
deduction_for_seed: No chain exists. The strongest statements that apply to the seed E unconditionally are: (A) Goldfeld2 Thm 1.2 + seed datum $E=E^{(1)}$, $a(E)\ge2$ (PROVED) => E lies in the density-zero exceptional set of its own twist family; conclusion C = 'the proportion of $d\in\mathcal D(X)$ with $a(E^{(d)})\ge2$ tends to 0'. This yields nothing about $\Sha(E/\Q)$, $a(E)$, $L''(E,1)$, or any $\Sha[p^\infty]$. (B) MeanRank Thm 1.2 + the same datum => the rank-weighted tail of the family is $\le C_E/R$ for $R\ge R_E\ge65537$; again a family-average statement with an inexplicit constant $C_E$, no pointwise content. (C) MeanRank Lemma tail:jensen gives $a(E^{(d)})\ll_E\log(3X)$, which at d=1 is an inexplicit upper bound on $a(E)$ -- the lab's numerical $L''(E,1)\ne0$ is already stronger evidence (though still not a proof that $a(E)=2$). To go from any of these to a seed obligation one would need a pointwise theorem for $s_p(E)=2$ (e.g. a rank-2 Gross--Zagier / derived-height formula, an IMC + control + height-nondegeneracy chain at the remaining primes 59, 487, 2243, 4547, 5843, or a cofinite Kato-divisibility estimate); none is present in the six manuscripts or anywhere in the 719 (sweep-overview negative result (1)). K-A: nothing above assumes Sha finite, $a(E)=2$, or BSD; nothing above produces them either. For E^{-7} the corank-0 theorems apply, but the deduction 'ExactBSD Thm 1.1 + $s_q(E^{-7})=0$ => BSD formula for E^{-7}' is the separate item twist-E-7 and is not a rank-2 statement.
